headline: AI selling is back but yields dropped after weak housing starts: NQ −0.5% pre-open, no clean edge
session_note: Cash open 9:30 AM ET (10:30 AM Atlantic) · morning window

flip.long: NDX gets back above Monday's close (29,529; NQ ≈ 29,720, flat on the day) and holds there after 9:30 while the 10-year stays below ~5.10%.
flip.short: NQ breaks the overnight low (~29,478) and NDX can't get back above Monday's low (29,461) in the first 30 min, especially if the 10-year rebounds above ~5.14% or Brent pushes further above $111.

thesis: Monday's AI-led bounce is fading. Nasdaq-100 futures were around 29,536–29,564 at 8:38–8:42 AM ET, down ~0.5–0.6% from Monday's 29,722.5 settle [1,7]. Chip and AI-infrastructure stocks are leading the drop again (Micron, Sandisk −3%, CoreWeave −4%+, SMH −1%) after Korea's Elice fell ~30% on its debut and the Kospi lost 3.7% [3,4,6]. Brent is at a five-month high above $110 on Houthi attacks on Saudi targets [4,6,13]. The offset came at 8:30 AM: September housing starts fell to **1.221M vs ~1.30M expected** (permits 1.400M vs 1.39M) [3,5]. The 10-year dropped to ~5.09% from Monday's 5.14% close, the dollar index eased to ~101.7, and NQ bounced ~120 points off its overnight low [7,10]. Markets price an October hike at only ~16–17% but still expect a December hike (Fed in blackout before Oct 27–28) [8,9,12]. Futures imply an open below Monday's NDX low (29,461). Weak AI sentiment points down, but falling yields push the other way, and Netflix/SpaceX don't report until after the close [4]. I lean bearish but **see no clean edge for the open**. Let the first 15–30 minutes decide.

bullets.label: The data is out and it softened yields.
bullets.text: September housing starts came in at 1.221M (−5.2% m/m) vs ~1.30M consensus, and single-family starts were 859K. Permits were 1.400M vs 1.39M. The 10-year fell to ~5.09% and NQ bounced ~120 points off its 8:30 AM low [3,5,7]. Pending home sales are due at 10:00 AM ET (consensus ~0.0%) [11].

bullets.label: AI risk-off is global this morning.
bullets.text: The Kospi fell 3.73% and SK Hynix 4.2%. European tech was down 1.4% and ABB fell ~6% despite record orders. In the US premarket, Micron, Sandisk, Intel and AMD were down 2–3%, CoreWeave/Nebius were down ~4–5%, and Apple was down ~1.2% [3,4,6].

bullets.label: Implied gap below Monday's low.
bullets.text: NQ traded ~193 points over cash NDX at Monday's settle (29,722.5 vs 29,529.35). On that basis ~29,550 NQ implies an NDX open near 29,355, just below Monday's 29,461 low and about halfway back down Monday's bounce from 29,188 [2,7]. That's an approximate basis estimate, not a quote.

bullets.label: No Fed or megacap catalyst before the close.
bullets.text: The Fed is in its quiet period before the Oct 27–28 FOMC. Netflix and SpaceX report after Tuesday's close, and Meta/Tesla report Wednesday. GM's −6–7% premarket drop (on a guidance narrowing) is only a small drag on the Nasdaq [3,4,12].

bullets.label: Bull case:
bullets.text: Yields are falling, not rising (−5 bp after the soft housing print), the dollar is weaker, and October hike odds are only ~16–17%. Nvidia is barely lower (−0.6%), and futures are already ~120 points off the overnight low. Gap-downs into Monday's range after a strong bounce often get bought, and dip buyers stepped in hard Monday [3,6,7,8].

bullets.label: Bear case:
bullets.text: Monday's bounce looks like a one-day relief rally. Selling is spreading from Asia and Europe into US chips, and CoreWeave's credit (distressed CDS, high Oracle bond yields) is still stressed. Brent at $110–111 keeps the inflation/December-hike story alive. A clean break of the overnight low would likely target Friday's 29,188 NDX close [3,4,6,13].

bullets.label: Flip to LONG:
bullets.text: NDX gets back above Monday's close (29,529; NQ ≈ 29,720) and holds it after 9:30 AM, with the 10-year staying below ~5.10% and chips (SMH) turning green. Stronger: the 10-year moves toward 5.05%.

bullets.label: Flip to SHORT:
bullets.text: NQ breaks the overnight low (~29,478, ≈ NDX 29,285) and NDX stays below Monday's low (29,461) through the first 30 minutes. Also counts: the 10-year rebounds through ~5.14% or Brent extends above ~$111.5 on Gulf/Houthi headlines.

bullets.label: Wildcards:
bullets.text: The 10:00 AM pending home sales print, any AI-financing or CoreWeave credit headline, unscheduled Fed/Warsh comments despite the blackout, and Middle East oil headlines [3,4,11].

data_notes: The NQ quotes are indicative (Markets Insider is from market makers; Yahoo may be delayed ~10 min). Snapshots disagree: CNBC showed NQ −0.8% at 8:28 AM and −0.4% at 8:44 AM ET. The NDX open implied from the ~193-pt futures premium is an estimate. The 10-yr ~5.09% is Yahoo's ^TNX at ~8:36 AM ET; other morning prints ran 5.12–5.145% before the housing data. WTI is muddied by the November contract expiring: the front Nov contract is ~$104 (CNBC $103.92), Dec is ~$99.8 (Yahoo CL=F), and Markets Insider shows $99.47 (−4%, a contract-roll artifact). The housing-starts consensus is ~1.30M per CNBC/Dow Jones. Pending home sales (10:00 AM) consensus ~0.0% comes from last week's Danske calendar and I couldn't re-verify it this morning. I didn't find any US Fed speakers today (blackout). Monday's NDX H/L/C were verified against Yahoo daily data.
